strings.name: Alicia Garza
strings.role: Movement organiser, writer and senior vice president at the Freedom Together Foundation
strings.summary: Alicia Garza co-founded Black Lives Matter with Patrisse Cullors and Opal Tometi. She founded Black Futures Lab and worked in women's and domestic workers' organising before moving into philanthropic funding as a senior vice president at the Freedom Together Foundation.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through 18 November 2026. Recent activity is supported by an account of her May MIT talk and a July programme article. Publication does not establish the recording date; co-founding a movement does not mean continuing to manage every related organisation.
strings.influence.rationale: Co-founded Black Lives Matter, advancing discussions of racial justice and public governance and helping generate social action across countries.
strings.facts.f1.label: Higher education
strings.facts.f1.value: Graduated from the University of California San Diego in 2002 after studying anthropology and sociology.
strings.facts.f2.label: Daily management and founder status
strings.facts.f2.value: In an interview, she said she left the Black Lives Matter Global Network's daily operations in 2017. Founder status does not establish a current management role.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Co-founding Black Lives Matter
strings.highlights.h1.text: Joined Cullors and Tometi in 2013 to advance an initiative against racial inequality and violence affecting Black communities. The movement developed through many local organisations and participants.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Building a platform for community research and organising
strings.highlights.h2.text: Founded Black Futures Lab, combining community surveys, organiser training and policy participation. The Black Census is a civil-society survey project, not the U.S. government census.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Programme article documented guest-hosting work
strings.timeline.t1.text: NewsOne published Rashad Robinson's account of her Freedom Table discussion with him and LaTosha Brown about organising and civic participation. The date shown is the article's publication date.
strings.timeline.t2.title: JPB Foundation announced appointment
strings.timeline.t2.text: The foundation announced her appointment as senior vice president of Movement Infrastructure and Explorations while she was transitioning from her previous role. JPB was renamed the Freedom Together Foundation in 2024.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Published The Purpose of Power
strings.timeline.t3.text: Published a book about organising and social movements. The publisher lists the ebook and audiobook release on this date, with the paperback following on 7 September 2021.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Co-founded Supermajority
strings.timeline.t4.text: Helped establish the women's political participation organisation with Cecile Richards, Ai-jen Poo and others. On 8 January 2026, it announced that it would no longer operate as a standalone organisation.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Founded Black Futures Lab
strings.timeline.t5.text: Launched a platform for policy participation and organising in Black communities and gathered community views through the Black Census Project.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Network she co-founded received Sydney Peace Prize
strings.timeline.t6.text: The Black Lives Matter Global Network received the prize. Patrisse Cullors, Rodney Diverlus and Dawn Modkins accepted it in person on the network's behalf.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Helped launch Black Lives Matter
strings.timeline.t7.text: After George Zimmerman's acquittal in the Trayvon Martin shooting case, worked with Patrisse Cullors and Opal Tometi to develop the initiative and organising network.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Graduated from UC San Diego
strings.timeline.t8.text: Completed undergraduate studies in anthropology and sociology, then became involved in community organising in the Bay Area.
